key_insight: A self-balancing sequential sampler adaptively biases choices to make empirical coverage converge as fast as possible while keeping future selections difficult to predict.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to reduce repeated picks and long gaps in scheduling, auditing, and treatment assignment without sacrificing randomness too much.
method: Use adaptive sampling probabilities that depend on current count imbalance.
Exploit a Markovian invariance property and a stochastic mirror-descent view.
Tune biasing strength to trade off convergence speed against predictability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an explicit theoretical guarantee of optimal O(n^-1) convergence, a uniqueness result from an entropy-regularized optimization problem, and an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusive limit under weak biasing.
watch_item: Performance depends on bias-parameter choice, so overly strong biasing may reduce unpredictability or make implementation sensitive to tuning.
paper_title: Self-Balancing Sequential Sampling: Fast Convergence with Controlled Predictability
